english.notes:
(i) Threatening' includes verbal and physical threats and violent conduct; 'Abusive' means degrading or reviling language;
'Insulting' means scornful, insolent, contemptuous; Behaviour must be directed against another person. There must be evidence that the suspect intended or was aware that his words or behaviour were or may have been threatening, abusive or insulting, and either:-
(i) he intended the 'victim' to believe immediate unlawful violence would be used against him or someone else by someone; or
(ii) he intended to provoke the 'victim' or another person into using immediate unlawful violence; or
(iii) the 'victim' was likely to believe that such violence would be used; or
(iv) it was likely that such violence would be provoked.
(v) This offence may take place in public or private, but not where both suspect and victim are inside dwellings (even different dwellings). Examples: throwing of missiles in public, where no injury is sustained; scuffles or incidents of violence or threats of violence committed in the context of a brawl, which fall short of Affray: incidents between neighbours or members of the public which do not justify assault charges; incidents where an individual is picked on by a gang, where an assault charge is not appropriate
(vi)See the CPS charging standards for this offence before preparing any charges.

other.penalty:
Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
